correctness.rationale: For the two embedded F2, t=1 differential tables a separate word/bit-matrix check verified degree -1, d^2=0, exactly the printed 4 and 2 integral-graded augmentations, 48 mod-2-graded augmentations per plat, the homotopy partitions (4), (2), and (16,16,16) for each mod-2 grading, and the indicated integral-graded linearized ranks. Independently tracing the plat strands gives one component on each side, consistent integer Maslov potentials and tb=1. Exhausting the normal ruling matchings gives switches {19,20,21,22} and {3,4,19,20,21,22} in each case, with grading gcd/exponent (0,0) and (4,2). I reproduced P2 from the actual first published grid by rotating and replaying local front moves. P1 is printed in the atlas braid table. This type is starred: row numbers alone do not identify the same entry. The atlas states that the braid representatives correspond to the displayed grid entries, possibly in a different order. In the four displayed entries the integral-graded polynomial t^(-4)+t+t^4 is unique (June 2026 atlas, p. 9); both plats belong to this finite list and have that polynomial, identifying the same entry within that list. This is not a general inference of Legendrian isotopy from matching invariants. No full Jones state sum or independent grid-to-grid isotopy sequence is claimed; smooth type follows from the atlas identification.
